upstream.name: zeta-23-lean
upstream.notice: derives files under Zeta23/FromPNTPlus/ from PrimeNumberTheoremAnd (Apache-2.0), some of which derive from mathlib (Apache-2.0); see upstream NOTICE

toolchain_note: Upstream pins one Lean release earlier and a different Mathlib commit. Section 11 permits an external formal dependency only after toolchain compatibility is proven; it has not been proven.
hash_note: Every statement_source_hash below is a whitespace-normalized hash of the declaration's source text at the pinned commit. It is a pin, not a statement comparison: an elaborated_statement_hash requires building Zeta23 under its own toolchain, which has not been done. Promoting any row from reference to dependency requires that build.
architecture_adopted: trusted statement layer written over Mathlib alone
solution layer that may import the implementation library
machine-checked comparison that the two describe the same proposition
a reproducible audit record of sorry count and axiom dependencies

theorems.statement_source_normalized: theorem rank_trace_ineq_two {P Q : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hP : P.PosSemidef) (hQ : Q.IsHermitian) {r b : ℕ} (hr : P.rank ≤ r) (hb : posIndex hQ ≤ b) : 2 * rtrace P + 4 * rtrace Q - 4 * (b : ℝ) - frobSq (P + Q) ≤ (r : ℝ)
theorems.relationship: the same theorem Atlas records as unproved: 2 tr P + 4 tr Q - 4b - ||P+Q||_F^2 <= r

theorems.statement_source_normalized: theorem rank_trace_ineq {P Q : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hP : P.PosSemidef) (hQ : Q.IsHermitian) {r b : ℕ} (hr : P.rank ≤ r) (hb : posIndex hQ ≤ b) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) : c * rtrace P - c ^ 2 / 4 * r + 2 * c * rtrace Q - c ^ 2 * b ≤ frobSq (P + Q)
theorems.relationship: the general c > 0 form; Atlas's runtime implements the c = 2 specialization

theorems.statement_source_normalized: theorem posIndex_eq_max_finrank_posDefOn {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) : ∃ W : Submodule 𝕜 (n → 𝕜), PosDefOn A W ∧ Module.finrank 𝕜 W = posIndex hA
theorems.relationship: identifies the eigenvalue-count and subspace formulations of the positive index; Atlas defines the index by the subspace form and does not need this

theorems.statement_source_normalized: theorem finrank_le_posIndex_of_posDefOn {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {W : Submodule 𝕜 (n → 𝕜)} (hW : PosDefOn A W) : Module.finrank 𝕜 W ≤ posIndex hA
theorems.relationship: the direction Atlas would need to bound an index from a witness subspace

theorems.statement_source_normalized: theorem posIndex_conj_le {Q : Matrix m m 𝕜} (hQ : Q.IsHermitian) (B : Matrix m d 𝕜) : posIndex (isHermitian_conjTranspose_mul_mul B hQ) ≤ posIndex hQ
theorems.relationship: one-sided bound for arbitrary B; applying it at B = S and B = S_inv gives Atlas's equality for invertible S

theorems.statement_source_normalized: theorem posIndex_add_le {Q₁ Q₂ : Matrix m m 𝕜} (hQ₁ : Q₁.IsHermitian) (hQ₂ : Q₂.IsHermitian) : posIndex (hQ₁.add hQ₂) ≤ posIndex hQ₁ + posIndex hQ₂
theorems.relationship: no Atlas counterpart yet; relevant to a block-sum argument in a higher-dimensional pilot
